 'We could've won the game' published at 22:22 GMT 22:22 GMT 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham midfielder Shea Charles speaking to Sky Sports : "Definitely. You could feel a shift in the second half. The way the goal came wasn't how we deserved it really, but positive signs. We could've won the game in the end, but a really good away performance."
 On the message from head coach Alvaro Arbeloa : "It was just to play how we can play. I thought we started quite slow. Giving the ball away in areas we didn't want to. I feel like them right where we wanted them on the press, but then they'd win a duel and be in on goal. I think when we tightened up and recycled the ball and started to play through them, we played really well."
 On teammate Calvin Bassey : "Top player. I don't want to big him up too much, but he's a really good leader. Especially for me coming into the league in my first season. There is no one better to have at the back."
 5 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We will support him' published at 22:17 GMT 22:17 GMT 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa defender Ian Maatsen speaking to Sky Sports: "We started the game well. Fulham is a good side, not easy to
win [against] but we came in front. We done well but in the second half we gave them more
time on the ball. They have good players and they can make chances. 
 "We were
unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It’s important not to lose
these games.
 On Suzuki's mistake for the goal: "It’s frustrating because don’t want to concede goals but it
can happen to everyone. 
 "Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn
from it. We will support him and go again."
 37 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A good away performance' published at 22:13 GMT 22:13 GMT 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey speaking to Sky Sports : "I think it was a good away performance. We know how hard it is to come here. It is a difficult place to come, a team with a lot of quality. We wanted a clean sheet, but proud of the boys. They did well."
 On whether they could have got three points instead of one : "I think we should have got more. We missed two chances inside the six-yard box. I know the boys are out there working their socks off to get in the right positions and finishing, we've just got to stay patient and keep trusting in them because we know the quality they have. I just think we could have took all three. A bit unlucky, but we've got to keep positive. Games like this, we've seen in the past where we've been drawing and we've lost. Ipswich, for example.If we can't win, it's very important we don't lose and just happy that we've progressed."
 On Fulham's current form : "100%. Since the start of the season, we've been improving each week and everyone all working hard. Everyone has bought into the way the manager wants to play. We're starting to learn and understand each other. Hopefully, things are going up from now."

 Image source, Press Association Image caption, Julio Enciso equalised with his second Premier League goal of the season
 By Sam Drury BBC Sport journalist Julio Enciso's thumping strike salvaged a point for Ipswich in an entertaining Premier League draw at Hull. 
 The Paraguayan attacking midfielder rifled a left-foot shot into the top corner from 20 yards with 16 minutes remaining to equalise for Ipswich and deny Hull a first win since August.
 Ipswich had led through Florentino Luis' powerful near-post strike as they dominated the first half at MKM Stadium.
 After a dismal first-half showing, Hull were a different side in the second 45 minutes and levelled through Tim Iroegbunam before Oli McBurnie's free-kick found the bottom right corner to give them the lead.
 The lead lasted only six minutes, though, and the Tigers have now gone seven league games without tasting victory, eight in all competitions.
 Despite that run, Sergej Jakirovic's have lost only two league games and remain in the top half of the table, above Gary O'Neil's Ipswich on goal difference.
 Having gone behind in the second half, Ipswich will be glad to come away with something, but their early dominance was such that they may still be frustrated not to take all three points.
 They thoroughly deserved the lead by the time Abdoul Ouattara beat a man and slipped in Florentino to hammer home the opener.
 Ipswich then briefly thought they had doubled their advantage from a corner, only for Enciso's header to be ruled out for a foul on McBurnie moments earlier.
 The deficit stayed at one and a much-improved Hull levelled just before the hour as McBurnie found Iroegbunam, who beat the offside trap and was bizarrely given all the time in the world by the Ipswich defence to amble into the box and lash past Christian Walton for his first Premier League goal.
 The Ipswich goalkeeper was beaten again 10 minutes later, albeit he may feel he could have done better, as McBurnie drove in a low free-kick from just outside the box.
 Hull were buoyant and the crowd were with them, but Enciso's sizzling strike ensured the points would be shared.
 Have your say on Hull's performance 
 What did you make of Ipswichs' display? 
 Analysis: Missed opportunity for both sides? 
 Figure caption, Sergej Jakirovic - post-match interview - Hull vs Ipswich
 For two promoted sides to be sitting on 11 points from nine games, safely in mid-table for now, there shouldn't be too much to grumble about.
 Yet, both Hull and Ipswich will feel slightly frustrated after a highly watchable draw in East Yorkshire.
 It is the kind of result that each will hope they don't come to rue at the end of the campaign.
 For Ipswich, what will irk O'Neil most is that Ipswich were unable to capitalise on such a strong first half.
 With better decision-making around the penalty area and a little more ruthlessness, they could have been out of sight.
 Meanwhile, a slow start - to put it mildly - will be at the heart of Hull's frustration. That and their failure to keep themselves in front, having fought back to lead.
 While Hull continue to pick up points, the damage is lessened. But the longer they go without a victory, the more urgent is their need to rediscover that winning feeling.
 For the time being, both sides can focus on the resilience they showed after falling behind and the latest point ticked off in the quest to stay in the top flight. The hope in both camps will be that they don't ultimately see this as two dropped.
